chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When a wall-enclosed garden contains different types of fruits, and some of them ripen, there is no objection to selling all of them."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling mixed fruits in an orchard before all of them have ripened?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that partial ripeness does not invalidate the sale of the entire orchard, thereby mitigating *gharar* (uncertainty) in mixed produce transactions. This principle is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for validating sales of heterogeneous goods where uniform ripening is not guaranteed, ensuring commercial stability.
